take.thing: Three square crops sit in a row, each with a part name and a one line benefit beneath.
take.why: It proves quality in the three places a buyer checks, back, seat and leg, without a spec table.

left_out: the fabric macro running off the edge
differences: Labels in a serif with an Inter benefit line
Crops come from our own piece
sources.removal: Quality becomes a claim in a paragraph.

take.thing: Each tile gets a one word name and a two word character, such as Warm. Enduring.
take.why: It gives craft a vocabulary a buyer can repeat without reading a paragraph.

differences: Used on parts of the piece, not on materials
sources.removal: The row reads as captions with no voice.

sources.family: Furniture Made to Belong UI card

take.thing: One of the three crops is a hand pressing the weave, so texture is felt not described.
take.why: A hand in the picture tells a buyer how soft or firm the cushion is.

left_out: the floating card over the photo
differences: Our crop is square and on ivory
The hand belongs to the client's maker
sources.removal: All three crops are still objects and nothing says touch.
